title: Soft quarantine and phased rejoin readiness to stabilize autoscaler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent readiness flapping during transient warmups (cold starts, network blips, GC pauses) causes the autoscaler to oscillate: rapid scale-downs followed by quick scale-ups. This increases tail latency, wastes dedicated capacity, and risks SLO burn. Existing readiness/liveness binary gating immediately removes nodes from the LB/autoscaler, but that reaction is too aggressive for transient failure modes and multi-region failover scenarios.

Proposal: Implement a 'soft quarantine' lifecycle state for instances that fail readiness without immediately triggering autoscale down or full traffic ejection. Nodes enter a phased quarantine with time-boxed diagnostics, synthetic warmup probes, progressive traffic fractioning, and a phased rejoin handshake. The autoscaler will consult a separate health-aggregation signal (quarantine score + synthetic warmup success) with hysteresis and dampening before issuing scale decisions. Integrate with per-route circuit-breakers so high-priority traffic can bypass quarantined nodes when necessary.

Goals: reduce autoscaler thrash, keep tail latency within SLOs during recoveries, reduce unnecessary instance churn and failed rollbacks during canaries, and provide transparent visibility for on-call and SREs.
acceptance_criteria: New lifecycle state 'QUARANTINED_SOFT' implemented and surfaced in console/telemetry
Autoscaler respects quarantine-derived health score: no scale-downs triggered by transient readiness failures within configured hysteresis window
Average scale events per 24h reduced by >= 40% for services observed to flap in prior incident playback
Tail P95/P99 latency remains within SLO during controlled failure injection tests (see test plan)
Canary rollouts do not auto-abort due to soft-quarantine transient events (configurable override)
rollout_plan: Step 1: implement health aggregation and quarantine state in staging; enable for a single low-traffic service
Step 2: run 72h canary on staging with fault injection (GC pause, delayed readiness) and monitor metrics
Step 3: expand to non-critical production services in a single region with increased observability
Step 4: enable multi-region-aware quorum for production services after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Rollback: feature flag off (immediate) — revert health aggregation only if increased SLO breaches observed
metrics: service.p95_latency and p99_latency during quarantine windows
implementation_notes: Add QUARANTINED_SOFT to instance lifecycle states; ensure LB routing supports traffic fractioning (0-100%) to this state
Health aggregator: combine readiness probe outcomes, synthetic warmup probe results, recent successful KV cache hits, and token-prioritized request samples into a quarantine score (0-100)
Hysteresis config: min_quarantine_duration (default 30s), max_quarantine_duration (default 10m), backoff_factor for repeated failures

Autoscaler integration: expose quarantine_score to autoscaler decision API. Autoscaler applies dampening: ignore scale-down if mean quarantine_score across group is > threshold or if within cooldown window
Circuit breaker integration: allow route-level override to mark quarantined nodes as excluded for certain critical token buckets; fallback to regional pool when critical traffic surges
Observability: surface quarantine state per-instance in console, enable timeline view, add synthetic_warmup traces and warmup-step logs
Config knobs for SRE: quarantine_score_thresholds, synthetic_probe_concurrency, traffic_fraction_step (e.g., 0%, 10%, 50%, 100%), and emergency_force_eject
Add unit/integration tests for state transitions, and chaos tests that emulate multi-region network partitions and verify no autoscaler thrash
Backward compatibility: if feature flag off, behavior is unchanged. Provide migration guide for Dedicated customers with custom autoscalers
testing_plan: Unit tests for quarantine state machine and score calculation
Integration test: simulated GC pause causes instance -> quarantined -> phased rejoin, assert no immediate scale-down
Chaos experiments: region partition and delayed rejoin; validate multi-region quorum gating prevents cascade failover
Load test: ramp traffic during phased rejoin and assert p99 latency stays within SLO
Canary rollout validation on non-prod then progressive increase to prod services
notes: Trade-offs: soft quarantine reduces sensitivity to transient failures at the cost of temporarily keeping partially degraded nodes in path. We mitigate risk with traffic fractioning and token-prioritized bypass.
Open questions: threshold defaults for quarantine_score and optimal synthetic warmup probe design (lightweight vs. representative), whether to include KV cache priming as a required warmup step
Follow-ups: tie quarantine behavior into cost analytics (show cost savings from reduced churn) and extend to dedicated autoscaler policies for Reserved pools
